assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which a single twist angle tunes flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity. It is a genuine surprise from quantum mechanics in a stable two-dimensional material, and it spawned the whole field of moire quantum matter. The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction paired with a clean experiment is the type of theory-experiment link I value.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. The three supplied names form a coherent theory plus experiment configuration. Experimental co-leaders such as Yuan Cao as first author are not on the credited list and so cannot be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Observed in many independent groups since 2018 and extended to other moire systems. The band-structure picture is firmly confirmed. The interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is robust and timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Credit between the experimental discovery and the earlier theoretical proposal could be debated; I am relying on my recollection of the history, not verified it independently.
Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's experimental group colleagues are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect established a new classification of quantum states by topology rather than symmetry breaking, with robust edge and surface states. It combines deep theory with first-principles electronic-structure calculations and spectroscopy, and ARPES confirmation of the surface Dirac cones. Its influence on condensed matter has been broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theoretical foundation of the Z2 quantum spin Hall idea; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells; Hasan's group observed 3D topological insulators by ARPES. A three-person prize cannot include Mele or others such as Zhang, Bernevig, or Fu, so some credit allocation is unavoidably awkward. I choose theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment.
assessment.maturity: Extensively and independently confirmed across materials and techniques over nearly two decades. Recognition is mature, perhaps overdue, though 2016 recognised topological phases generally.
uncertainties: The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases overlaps conceptually, which could make some members regard this as already covered.
Excluding Mele and the Zhang-Bernevig theory work leaves a contentious attribution.
Many contributors beyond the four credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later giant TMR with crystalline MgO barriers, underlie modern read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The physics rests on spin-dependent tunnelling and, in the MgO case, symmetry-selective coherent tunnelling that was predicted by first-principles electronic-structure calculations and then confirmed. It is real use grounded in a clear physical discovery, and follows the 2007 GMR prize naturally.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin (and Yuasa and Djayaprawira in parallel) demonstrated giant TMR with MgO in 2004. The theory of coherent tunnelling by Butler and by Mathon and Umerski is not credited here and arguably should be. The three supplied names form a reasonable though imperfect trio.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, independently reproduced and commercially deployed for over fifteen years. Timeliness is good, even late.
uncertainties: Priority between the Japanese and American groups and the MgO groups (Yuasa, Djayaprawira) is partly unresolved.
Theory contributions that explain the giant effect are not among the credited names.
Some members may see it as a continuation of the GMR prize rather than a new discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, explaining the Mott transition and, combined with DFT, enabling quantitative calculations of real correlated materials. It is exactly the interface between model theory and materials spectroscopy, and I know it well from my own field. It has shaped experimental interpretation of spectra for transition-metal oxides, heavy fermions and actinides.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit; Georges and Kotliar formulated the mapping to an impurity problem and the DMFT approach; Kotliar also drove the LDA+DMFT extension. Walter Metzner and Marcelo Rozenberg, Krauth and Kajueter are outside the credited names, so the prize configuration omits an originator. I choose the three supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of application and benchmarking, but quantitative predictive accuracy varies by system and the impurity-solver and double-counting choices are still contested in LDA+DMFT.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner, who co-founded the infinite-dimension limit, is a real attribution problem.
Predictive quality of realistic DMFT calculations is system-dependent.
A theory-method prize without a single decisive experimental discovery may be viewed as less typical for the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned fundamental many-body models into controllable laboratory systems. The observation of the superfluid-to-Mott insulator transition and later single-site resolved Fermi-Hubbard physics provide direct, quantitative access to physics that is hard for theory and computation. It builds on the earlier cold-atom prizes and is a significant conceptual advance.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) provided the theoretical proposal; Greiner and Bloch realised the Mott transition and developed quantum-gas microscopy; Esslinger realised fermionic Mott insulators. Five names are credited, so a three-person selection necessarily leaves out Esslinger, Cirac and Jaksch. I choose a pairing of theory and bosonic experiment.
assessment.maturity: The Mott transition result is firmly confirmed; the broader aim of resolving open questions of the Fermi-Hubbard model such as pseudogap or d-wave pairing is still unfinished, so part of the promise is not yet realised.
uncertainties: Five credited names cannot fit a three-person prize; Esslinger and Cirac are left out.
Whether quantum simulation has yet produced decisive new physics, versus validation, remains open.
Dominant credit between Bloch and Greiner given the Hansch-group and Munich history is something I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO, rapidly raised above 50 K, produced the second family of high-temperature superconductors and a major new platform of multiband, magnetic and nematic physics. It was a surprise, and electronic-structure calculations have been central to understanding the Fermi surfaces and magnetism.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the discovery, with Kamihara as first author of the 2008 paper; the two-name configuration is clear and unusually clean. Rapid follow-up work by Chinese groups raised the transition temperature but the original discovery is not in dispute.
assessment.maturity: Discovery is thoroughly confirmed and the materials class is well established. The pairing mechanism is still unresolved, and the highest transition temperatures lie below the cuprates, so some members may judge the impact smaller.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism remains unresolved.
Practical impact has been limited relative to the cuprates.
Credit for the follow-on higher-Tc compounds is spread across other groups not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, using the magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy, and a possible redefinition of the second. Quantitatively impressive, reproducible, and well verified across laboratories.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye's group pushed them to the highest precision and made the many-body and Sr clock innovations. A two-person configuration is natural, though the 2005 prize on frequency combs and the 2012 prize on ion trapping overlap in field and some members may see it as another precision-metrology prize.
assessment.maturity: Mature and robustly replicated across many groups worldwide, with the redefinition of the second pending, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Contribution of Peik, Hollberg, Hall and others to optical clocks more broadly is outside the credited set.
Prior prizes in precision metrology may reduce appetite; this is outside my own field and I defer to atomic-physics colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron microscopy gave sub-angstrom resolution of atoms in materials and made quantitative atomic-resolution imaging and spectroscopy routine, which is directly valuable for the materials and spectroscopy community in which I work. The instrumentation changed what can be seen in solids, interfaces and defects, and comparisons with first-principles theory are now standard.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theory of the corrector; Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the hexapole corrector and its application in the late 1990s, with Kabius and Uhlemann as important co-workers who are not credited. The three supplied names form the standard trio recognised by the Kavli Prize in 2020 and so the configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial instruments worldwide and thousands of results, but as an instrumentation prize it must be weighed against the usual preference for discovery of a physical phenomenon.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as physics versus engineering instrumentation is uncertain.
Credit of the scanning-TEM Cs-corrector side (Krivanek, Dellby) is not among the credited names.
